data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Coupling school generative capacity to an exponentially decaying function of unretired criticism debt will constrain the runaway growth of rival positions from ~60 back to a sustainable equilibrium by forcing schools to resolve coverage debt before spawning new rivals.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Schools exploit the decay by generating trivial, easily-dismissed counter-criticisms to artificially lower their debt while preserving their rival positions.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The decay rate is miscalibrated, collapsing the diversity of rival positions below the threshold required for effective ensemble reasoning.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The computational overhead of recalculating the Dung grounded extension on every generative step with a dynamically changing debt threshold introduces an unacceptable latency.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The current architecture separates generation (via variator) from criticism (via Dung grounded extensions) without a feedback loop forcing generation to pause for criticism. By introducing a decay coefficient that scales the allowed bounded edits (from variator \u00b5) inversely with the volume of outstanding unaddressed warrants, schools will be locally forced to settle or retire existing arguments before generating new ones, preventing the asymmetry observed where rivalry grows unchecked.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
